title: SLO-aware preemption and fairness for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching improves throughput by aggregating in-flight tokens across requests, but it increases scheduling complexity when strict latency SLOs and multi-tenant fairness are required. Preemption is needed to meet low-latency SLOs for high-priority short requests, but naive preemption increases GPU memory churn (KV cache eviction, context reconstructions) and can harm long-running chat sessions. Goal: implement an SLO-aware scheduling layer that provides preemption and weighted fairness across tenants while minimizing KV cache damage and GPU memory fragmentation. Constraints: must integrate with existing KV cache snapshot API (ENG-7365), support per-customer SLOs/priority tiers, respect dedicated pool isolation, and run efficiently inside our serving runtime without adding large scheduling overhead. Success metrics: p99 latency for P0 short requests <= 120ms in steady-state under 3x load; overall token throughput degradation <= 8% vs baseline; KV cache hit-rate drop <= 5% for any tenant after preemption-enabled rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler exposes per-queue SLO and weight configuration and respects them during continuous batching
Preemption can interrupt/break batches to prioritize SLO-bound requests with bounded overhead (avg extra tokens processed per preemption < 50)
KV cache snapshots or incremental save/restore used to avoid full-model context reconstruction on preemption
End-to-end benchmark dashboard shows p50/p90/p99 latency per-priority under synthetic mixed workloads
Feature gated and rolloutable via runtime feature flag; canary on 5% nodes, ramp to 50% before full rollout
Security review completed for snapshot persistence behavior (if any)
design_decisions: Use a two-level scheduler: fast local admission that assigns requests into priority queues (short vs long, SLO buckets), and a slower global balancer for fairness across workers.
Preemption policy: token-quanta preemption where short SLO requests can steal headroom by preempting long-running batches at token boundaries, minimizing partial tensor writes and KV reorg.

KV strategy: lightweight incremental KV checkpointing at configurable token intervals (default 16 tokens) to allow efficient rollback/restore without full context rebuild. This integrates with ENG-7365 snapshots API.
Fairness: weighted deficit-round-robin across tenant-queues with decay for staleness, weights derived from customer tier + observed request rates.
Memory model: implement a soft-reservation layer for worst-case KV size per session; preemption must attempt to reuse existing reserved slots to avoid fragmentation and repeated GPU allocations.
Fallback: when preemption would cause >10% expected KV hit rate loss for a tenant, default to graceful degradation policy (return busy error or route to lower-cost model variant).
implementation_notes: Add new scheduler component in runtime/scheduler/slo_scheduler.cc with minimal cross-thread locking (use per-core queues + MPSC handoffs).
Extend request metadata to include slo_bucket and weight (numeric) for scheduling decisions; update REST/SDK layer to accept opt-in per-request SLO hints (backwards compatible).
Implement token-quanta preemption by marking a batch boundary and using existing batch executor interruption points; do not attempt mid-kernel preemption.
KV snapshot integration: call kv::Snapshot::prepare_for_preempt(session_id, token_index) which is provided by ENG-7365. If snapshot latency > 3ms, fall back to conservative non-preemptive path.
Add metrics: preemptions_total, preemption_latency_ms, preemptions_by_tenant, avg_kv_snapshot_ms, kv_hitrate_change_by_tenant. Hook into Console dashboard.
Unit tests for scheduler invariants, e2e bench harness in infra/bench/slo_preempt_bench with mixed short/long traces.
test_plan: Unit tests: validate weighted fairness via deterministic queue injection tests
Integration: end-to-end smoke with kv snapshots mocked vs real KV service
Performance: run mixed workload bench (70% long chat, 30% short SLO-generations) at 1/2/3x baseline qps and collect p50/p90/p99, throughput, and KV hit-rate
Fault-injection: simulate KV snapshot failures and high snapshot latency to ensure graceful fallback
Canary: deploy to 5% runtime nodes, enable feature flag, monitor the dashboard for 48h before ramping
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature flag behind runtime flag slo_preempt_v1. Internal testing in staging clusters. (owner: Marco Li)
Phase 2: Canary on 5% of prod nodes for 72h, monitor p99 latencies and kv hit-rate, rollback if p99 increases >10ms or kv hit-rate drop >3% for any tenant.
Phase 3: Ramp to 25% for 7 days, compare against control cohort; if stable, 50% for 7 days.
Phase 4: Full rollout with follow-up postmortem and opt-out knobs per-customer (control plane toggle).
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after RFC sync. Initial ask from Growth: reduce P0 short request p99 during peak. Spike to evaluate preemption strategies assigned.

2026-02-16 Marco Li: Spike complete. Found two viable approaches: (A) token-quanta preemption with KV snapshots, (B) speculative short-path fast-tracks that bypass batching for <32-token requests. Approach A chosen due to better throughput preservation. Notes and microbench results in design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/123456789/SLO-aware+Batching+Design

2026-02-20 Dev: Prototype implemented token-quanta preemption in a branch. Simple bench (1 GPU, 3x mixed load) showed P0 p99 improved from 320ms -> 95ms, but KV hit-rate dropped 14% for long sessions. Need KV snapshot integration to reduce hit-rate loss.

2026-02-25 Engineering review: Feedback from storage team (Priya) - snapshots must avoid synchronous CPU->GPU copies; suggested async pinned staging buffer and reuse pool. Added dependency ENG-7365 for snapshot API improvements.

2026-03-01 Marco Li: Integrated ENG-7365 snapshot API. Snapshot median latency in microbench: 1.6ms, 95th 3.2ms. After integration, KV hit-rate drop reduced to ~3.8% in bench; throughput loss 6.5% vs baseline. Meets acceptance targets in prelim tests.

2026-03-04 PM review (Jonah): Please add per-tenant opt-out and ensure dedicated pools do not get preempted. Also request more conservative default weights for enterprise tiers. Added to implementation notes.

2026-03-08 QA: Added e2e bench harness with real-world traces (support chat corpus). Observed rare edge-case where repeated preemptions cause memory fragmentation over long runs. Hypothesis: allocator churn from KV slot resizing. Action: implement soft-reservation for KV slots and periodic compaction. Tagged ENG-7450 as follow-up.

2026-03-10 Security (Maya): Confirmed snapshot retention policy is ephemeral, no persisted PII. Security review completed. Note: add audit log entry when snapshot is used for preemption (logged at INFO).

2026-03-12 Marco Li: Preparing canary deployment manifests and console dashboard panels (preemptions_total, avg_kv_snapshot_ms, p99_by_priority). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8452. Requesting review from Priya and Jonah.
